sections.h2: Where is Halifax County, Virginia, and what is in it?
sections.html:
Halifax County is on Virginia's southern border with North Carolina, and its county seat is the town of Halifax. South Boston is the largest town. At 830 square miles, of which 818 are land, it is one of the larger counties in the state by area.

It borders Campbell, Charlotte, Mecklenburg and Pittsylvania counties in Virginia, and Granville, Person and Caswell counties in North Carolina. U.S. 58, U.S. 360 and U.S. 501 cross the county, along with a long list of state routes.

Incorporated towns are Halifax, Scottsburg, South Boston and Virgilina. Census-designated places include Clover, Cluster Springs, Mountain Road, Nathalie and Riverdale. Smaller communities include Alton, Cody, Crystal Hill, Turbeville and Vernon Hill.

sections.h2: What is the history of Halifax County?
sections.html:
English colonists established the county in 1752 from Lunenburg County and named it for George Montagu-Dunk, the 2nd Earl of Halifax. Indigenous peoples had lived in the area for thousands of years before that.

One piece of local history affects paperwork. South Boston was an independent city through the 1990 census, then became a town again and rejoined Halifax County in 1995. If a seller has older records mentioning the city of South Boston, ask the Commissioner of the Revenue which office holds the parcel today.

Wikipedia's county article pictures a tobacco barn on Edgewood Farm. The county peaked at 41,442 residents in the 1950 census and has declined since, falling from 37,355 in 2000 to 34,022 in 2020.

sections.h2: How many people live in Halifax County, and what does that mean for housing?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 34,022 residents, and the Census Bureau's 2025 estimate is 33,447. The housing numbers: 17,275 housing units, 14.9% vacant, and 70.8% of occupied homes owner-occupied.

  • Median age was 47.7 years, and 25.2% of residents were 65 or older.
  • About 33.3% of households were one person living alone.
  • 21.8% of residents lived in urban areas and 78.2% in rural areas.

A county with older owners, many single-person households and a falling population tends to produce estate sales and vacant houses. If you have inherited a Halifax County house you do not plan to keep, the tax bill still arrives every year.

sections.h2: What schools and local government serve Halifax County?
sections.html:
Halifax County Public Schools is the school division. The county is run by a Board of Supervisors with eight districts plus a tie-breaker seat, and it has the usual constitutional offices: the Clerk of the Circuit Court, the Commissioner of the Revenue, the Treasurer, the Sheriff and the Commonwealth's Attorney.

For a house sale, the offices that matter are the Commissioner of the Revenue, the Treasurer and the Clerk, who records deeds.

sections.h2: Who bills real estate tax in Halifax County?
sections.html:
The Treasurer collects, and the Commissioner of the Revenue is the chief tax authority who keeps real estate ownership information. Both offices are at 1030 Mary Bethune Street in Halifax.

  • Treasurer: Suite 103, phone 434-476-3318, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:30 p.m.
  • Commissioner of the Revenue: Suite 104, phone 434-476-3314, open Monday to Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 5 p.m.

The Treasurer's page lists 2026 rates of $0.50 per $100 of value for real estate, $3.85 for personal property and $1.26 for machinery and tools.

Payment fees are posted there too: a 2.50% convenience charge on credit and debit cards, with a $2.00 minimum, and a $1.50 flat fee for eCheck payments.

sections.h2: When are Halifax County real estate taxes due?
sections.html:
Real estate tax payments are due June 5 and December 5. For 2026, the Treasurer posted a notice that bills would be mailed after the tax rate was approved on June 1, 2026, and the due date was extended to June 29, 2026.

Personal property and machinery and tools are due December 5. We did not open a page stating the Halifax penalty and interest rates, so ask the Treasurer for them, along with a payoff figure if the house is under contract.

The Treasurer's page also links to a list titled Sale of Valuable Real Estate for November 2026, which is dated 09/23/26 to 10/07/26 in the directory. Ask the Treasurer what that list covers, and call right away if your parcel number appears on it.

sections.h2: What tax relief does Halifax County offer?
sections.html:
The Commissioner's page describes a Real Estate Tax Relief Program that gives a discount on tax bills to elderly or permanently disabled owners who meet income and net worth tests. The discount applies to the house and up to one acre of land.

  • The applicant must be 65 or permanently and totally disabled on December 31 of the prior year.
  • The applicant must own and live in the home on that date.
  • The page lists gross combined income of no more than $22,000, with income of relatives living in the house counted above $8,500.
  • The page lists net worth of no more than $60,000, not counting the house and one acre.

These limits are printed on the county page as posted, and a county can change them, so confirm with the Commissioner before you rely on them. The same office also has forms for a disabled veteran real estate tax exemption and for a land use program.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Halifax County assessment?
sections.html:
The Commissioner's page links a 2026 Real Estate Assessment Appeal Application, so start there. We did not find a page on that site stating the filing deadline or the board of equalization schedule, so ask the Commissioner at 434-476-3314 how many days you have from your notice.

Virginia also lets a person assessed by a commissioner of the revenue request a correction within three years of the end of the tax year or one year from the assessment date, whichever is later, when the error was the commissioner's or came from a factual mistake in a general reassessment.

sections.h2: How is unpaid tax handled when a Halifax County house sells?
sections.html:
Under the Code of Virginia, the lien for real estate taxes comes before every other lien and stays until the taxing authority is paid. The statute says the purchaser or a foreclosure trustee must see that sale proceeds go toward taxes, including penalties and interest.

At a normal closing, the title company asks the Treasurer for a payoff and pays it from the seller's proceeds. Ask the Treasurer for the figure in writing and check whether the second half is already billed.

sections.h2: What do sellers in Halifax County usually face?
sections.html:
Common situations include inherited farmhouses, rental houses with tenants, vacant homes in smaller towns and houses needing repairs. With 14.9% of housing units vacant in 2020, empty houses are a real part of the local housing stock.

We buy Halifax County houses as-is, and unpaid real estate tax is paid from the proceeds at closing.

faqs.q: What is the Halifax County real estate tax rate for 2026?
faqs.a: The Treasurer's page lists $0.50 per $100 of value for real estate in 2026.

faqs.q: When are Halifax County real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: June 5 and December 5. For 2026 the Treasurer extended the first due date to June 29, 2026 because bills were mailed after the June 1 rate vote.

faqs.q: Who do I call about a Halifax County assessment?
faqs.a: Call the Commissioner of the Revenue at 434-476-3314. Call the Treasurer at 434-476-3318 for balances and payments.

faqs.q: Does Halifax County offer tax relief for seniors?
faqs.a: Yes. The Commissioner's page describes a program for owners 65 or older or permanently disabled who meet income and net worth limits, covering the house and up to one acre.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Halifax County house that has back taxes?
faqs.a: Yes. The lien is paid from the sale proceeds at closing, so request a payoff from the Treasurer before the closing date.
